subject: Genetics
title: Universal DNA Databases
description: A quick win: understand Universal DNA Databases.

hook.text: What if everyone's DNA was in the database? Every crime with biological evidence would be solvable. Every single one.

buildup.text: Kuwait briefly passed a universal DNA law in 2015. Every citizen and visitor would be profiled. It was struck down.

discovery.text: A universal database eliminates racial bias in collection. Everyone is equally searchable. Fair by design.

twist.text: But it also means total genetic surveillance. Governments could track family ties, health risks, and ancestry.

climax.text: The trade-off is stark: solve every crime or protect everyone's privacy. No society has chosen the first—yet.

punchline.text: Solve every crime. Lose all genetic privacy. Pick one.

quiz.question: Why was Kuwait's universal DNA database law struck down?
